artifacts.name: About this indicator
artifacts.summary: Maps off- and on-street car parking — surface lots, multi-storey and underground garages and street-side parking — and measures how densely it is provided. A high parking supply is a signal of car-oriented urban design and of land given over to cars rather than to people.
artifacts.description: Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: parking_density · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Car parks explorer
artifacts.summary: The actual OpenStreetMap objects behind the car parks, with their attributes. Zoom in to inspect them.
artifacts.description:
The true OpenStreetMap geometry of every counted feature — points, ways and areas — carrying its name and (where mapped) opening hours. It appears from a neighbourhood zoom level so you can inspect the individual objects rather than an aggregate.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: parking_density · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Hot-spots & cold-spots
artifacts.summary: Global Moran’s I = 0.06. 3 hot-spot and 0 cold-spot neighbourhood(s) of car parks density (local Moran’s I / LISA). Only 15 sub-areas: too few for the permutation test to establish significance, so read a grey map as "not enough units to tell", not as "no clustering". Use a finer `subarea_mode` or a larger area to make this map informative. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
Sub-areas classified by the local Moran’s I statistic (LISA) over car parks density: **High-High** = a dense neighbourhood surrounded by others like it (hot-spot); **Low-Low** = a sparse one among others like it (cold-spot); **High-Low / Low-High** = spatial outliers. Significance uses a deterministic permutation test; non-significant sub-areas are greyed out.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: parking_density · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Hot-spots & cold-spots (per capita)
artifacts.summary: Global Moran’s I = -0.05. 0 hot-spot and 1 cold-spot neighbourhood(s) of car parks per 1,000 residents (local Moran’s I / LISA). Use a finer `subarea_mode` or a larger area to make this map informative. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
Sub-areas classified by the local Moran’s I statistic (LISA) over car parks per 1,000 residents: **High-High** = a well-supplied neighbourhood surrounded by others like it (hot-spot); **Low-Low** = a poorly-supplied one among others like it (cold-spot); **High-Low / Low-High** = spatial outliers. Significance uses a deterministic permutation test; non-significant sub-areas are greyed out.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: parking_density · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Average parking provision

artifacts.description:
Map algebra: for each administrative sub-area, the per-km² densities of the input categories are combined by **mean** — 1×Multi-storey car parks, 1×Underground car parks, 1×Surface car parks, 1×Marked parking spaces — into a single value. Use it to express a composite index (e.g. a weighted suitability score) as one layer instead of several.

artifacts.name: Distance to nearest car park
artifacts.summary: How far to the nearest car park from anywhere in the area (metres). Darker = further. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:

artifacts.name: Data currentness

artifacts.description:
Each point is a feature, shaded by the number of years since its last OpenStreetMap edit (measured against the data snapshot). Clusters of dark points mark areas where the OSM picture is ageing and may warrant a re-survey — a spatial companion to the data-quality note.
